title: DOTr ensures regular transport operations amid 'habagat'-induced heavy rains
content_lead:
MANILA, Philippines -- The Department of Transportation (DOTr) inspected major public transport facilities in Metro Manila on Wednesday to ensure the continued and safe movement of passengers amid heavy rains brought by the southwest monsoon or 'habagat.'

title: Bambike tour: Where to bike inside Quezon Memorial Circle
content_lead:
Looking for a safe space to take the whole family for biking around Quezon City?

While Quezon Memorial Circle has always been open to cyclists, those who don't have their own bikes can now rent bamboo bicycles inside the public park.

PHOTO BY Kara Santos

Visitors can now rent Bambike units every Saturday to explore QMC on their own or join the guided historical bike tours on select dates. While you can easily stroll around the park, renting a bike offers another fun way to explore, especially for those looking for something new to do or have always wanted to try riding a bamboo bicycle, which are popular for bike tours around Intramuros.

We frequently cycle around the area using our own bikes, but we recently took the free guided Bambike tour just to see what to expect. Bambike QC currently has 20 bamboo bicycle units for rent, including two-seater ones and a few for kids. Regular rental rates range from P100 to P220 per hour, but special discounts are given to QCID holders.

PHOTO BY Quezon Heritage House

The free guided bike tour combines museum visits with a bit of bike exploration. It takes visitors around the four main museums inside Quezon Memorial Circle, as well as some scenic spots and landmarks, weather permitting. Throughout the 1.5-hour-long tour, you'll be in the company of Bambike Ecotours staff who guide you to designated areas around the park, share historical facts as you go around, keep an eye on the bikes when you go inside the museums, and help take souvenir photos.

PHOTO BY Quezon Heritage House

If you've already visited the museums inside QMC and just want to enjoy the great outdoors, we recommend renting or bringing your own bikes. But if you want to learn more about the history of Quezon City and go around on two wheels instead of walking, then you may want to join the guided tour.

Take note: The free guided bike tours are held every first and third Saturday of the month, and only for the first 10 visitors (first come, first served).

title: Food stocks secure after East Nusa Tenggara Quake, Bulog says
content_lead:
Jakarta (ANTARA) - Indonesia's state logistics agency, Bulog, says food reserves in East Nusa Tenggara remain secure to support earthquake-stricken communities during ongoing emergency response and recovery efforts, with tens of thousands of tons on standby.

Bulog President Director Ahmad Rizal Ramdhani said the province holds between 35,000 and 37,000 metric tons of rice, which is sufficient for immediate relief operations.

"Stocks are secure," Rizal said on Monday. "If more is needed, we will increase supplies."

Bulog is distributing rice across East Nusa Tenggara (NTT) to supply impacted areas without disrupting normal commercial distribution.

Local branch offices in affected districts and municipalities have been ordered to keep at least 20 metric tons of rice ready for immediate dispatch.

Each area will also receive an additional 1,000 liters of MinyaKita-branded government-subsidized cooking oil to support emergency public kitchens.

To mitigate logistical bottlenecks caused by damaged infrastructure, Bulog is preparing backup shipments from neighboring West Nusa Tenggara and South Sulawesi.

"Challenging geography and limited communications in some areas prompted us to prepare larger reserves than currently identified needs," Rizal said.

He noted that Bulog began dispatching emergency aid before receiving formal requests from regional authorities to ensure evacuees in temporary shelters received immediate assistance.

"The TNI and local authorities are coordinating closely, and aid distribution in NTT is proceeding as planned," Rizal said, emphasizing that adequate food stocks will help accelerate long-term recovery for affected residents.

The OCTA survey revealed that controlling the increase in the prices of basic goods and services remains the country's most urgent national concern, cited by 37 percent of respondents. Although this represents an 8-percentage-point decline from 45 percent in March, inflation continues to top the public agenda, underscoring that the cost of living remains a pressing issue for many Filipino households.

Closely following inflation is the demand for higher wages and salaries, cited by 34 percent of respondents, virtually unchanged from the previous quarter. On the eve of this occasion, it is worth asking a simple question: What makes a friendship last? For Israel and the Philippines, the answer begins long before ambassadors presented credentials or governments signed agreements. It began with moral courage.

It is fitting that we celebrate Friendship Day in the month Filipinos honor the late President Manuel L. Quezon. Less than a decade later, the Philippines voted in favor of the establishment of the State of Israel at the United Nations. These were not merely diplomatic decisions. title: Advancing digital safety and responsible web behavior in Capiz and Quezon schools
content_lead:
Globe brought its Digital Thumbprint Program (DTP) to Sigma, Capiz, and Tayabas, Quezon, equipping youth leaders and school heads with the knowledge and skills to promote safer, more responsible online behavior. Through the initiative, Globe is expanding digital citizenship education beyond the classroom by empowering community and education leaders to champion digital safety where it matters most.

Building on its previous DTP engagements with more than 650 youth and student participants in Western Visayas earlier this year, Globe conducted a follow-through session in Sigma, Capiz, to complete its training for the municipality's remaining Sangguniang Kabataan (SK) officials and recent graduates. In Quezon, Globe also conducted DTP sessions for school heads representing municipalities across the province, strengthening their capacity to promote digital citizenship, cybersecurity awareness, and responsible AI use in schools.

"Young leaders have the ability to influence how their communities embrace technology. By equipping them with practical knowledge on digital safety, we are investing in a generation that can help create a safer and more responsible online environment for everyone. We hope they will share these lessons with their fellow youth and inspire more Filipinos to become responsible digital citizens," said Jun Juada, Globe Director for Western Visayas.

More than 30 SK officials and recent graduates participated in the follow-through session under Globe's #GoSafeWithGlobe campaign in Sigma, while 41 school heads from 25 public schools representing municipalities across Quezon Province joined the training. The sessions equipped participants to protect personal information, recognize online threats, promote responsible technology use, and foster safer digital environments in their communities and schools.

"This training gave me practical knowledge that I can immediately apply in my daily life and share with fellow youth members in our barangay. As an SK official, I have a responsibility to help create a safer online environment by encouraging others to practice responsible digital behavior," said Ramel Baclor Flores, SK Chairperson of Barangay Poblacion Sur, Municipality of Sigma, Capiz.

The Tayabas session also strengthened the capacity of school heads to guide teachers and learners in responsible technology use as schools continue to integrate digital tools into teaching and learning.

"Preparing our school leaders for today's digital landscape is essential to creating safe and responsible learning environments. Through Globe's Digital Thumbprint Program, our school heads are better equipped to guide teachers and learners in practicing responsible digital citizenship and making informed use of technology," said Celedonio Balderas Jr., Schools Division Superintendent, City of Tayabas.

Now in its 10th year, Globe's award-winning Digital Thumbprint Program continues to evolve to address emerging online challenges. Since its launch in 2016, the initiative has reached over 4,100 schools, engaged 115,394 teachers, and provided access to more than two million students and educators nationwide.

"School leaders are among our strongest partners in promoting responsible digital citizenship. By investing in their digital readiness, we hope to empower more school communities to embrace technology safely, confidently, and responsibly," said Adonis Evangelista, Globe General Manager for South Luzon.

Through the Digital Thumbprint Program and the #GoSafeWithGlobe campaign, Globe continues to work with schools, local government units, and community organizations to equip more Filipinos with the knowledge and confidence to thrive safely in the digital world. Learn more at https://www.globe.com.ph/about-us/sustainability/learning/digital-thumbprint.

For more information about Globe, visit www.globe.com.ph.
